text:
Marathon Petroleum recovered 2.9% today after three straight days of losses, bouncing back as oil prices stabilized. The stock had fallen sharply from October 19 to 23 during peak Middle East tensions (when Brent crude hit $116), but today's move reflects a modest de-escalation: news that Saudi Arabia and Iran's leadership met to reduce tensions, combined with oil prices pulling back slightly, took some of the geopolitical risk premium out of the market. At $107.89 for U.S. crude, prices remain elevated but have retreated from their recent highs.

Refiners like Marathon benefit from both high oil prices and the ability to run plants at full capacity—which sits at 93.4% currently—converting crude into fuels. The volatility over the past week shows how tightly refining stocks move with Middle East supply risks: when tensions spike, crude surges and refiners gain; when de-escalation talk emerges, prices cool and the stock retraces. Today's recovery suggests investors are taking the Tehran meeting as a sign that supply disruptions are less imminent than they appeared just days ago.
